title: RAJUK Occupancy Certificate, Fire Safety License & BNBC 2020 Compliance Law (BD)
metaTitle: RAJUK Occupancy Certificate, BNBC & Fire License BD
metaDescription: Bangladesh legal rules for RAJUK plan approval, Occupancy Certificate, Fire License & BNBC 2020 safety compliance for Dhaka flats, offices, and factories.
keywords: flat occupancy certificate utility connection dhaka
heroIntro: Buying a flat or leasing commercial office space in Dhaka, Chattogram, or Gazipur without checking statutory building compliance can lead to sudden DESCO, Titas, or WASA utility disconnection, municipal sealing, or denied property insurance. Under the Building Construction Act, 1952, Dhaka Imarat Nirman Bidhimala 2008, Bangladesh National Building Code (BNBC) 2020, and the Fire Prevention and Extinction Act, 2003, developers and building owners carry strict statutory duties.

quickAnswer.heading: At a Glance: Building Compliance, Occupancy & Fire Law (BD)
quickAnswer.text: Constructing or occupying a multi-storey building in Bangladesh requires both an approved design permit and a post-completion Occupancy Certificate under Building Construction Rules, alongside BNBC 2020 safety compliance and an annual Fire Service License for commercial premises before legally transferring flats or operating offices.
points: Governing Laws: Building Construction Act 1952, Dhaka Imarat Nirman Bidhimala 2008, BNBC 2020 & Fire Prevention Act 2003
Occupancy Certificate: Mandatory before occupying a completed multi-storey building or connecting permanent utilities
Fire Safety NOC & License: Compulsory from Fire Service & Civil Defence for commercial, factory, hospital & high-rise premises
Buyer Protection: Real Estate Development and Management Act 2010 penalizes developers for unauthorized plan deviations

sections.h2: RAJUK Plan Approval vs. Mandatory Occupancy Certificate
sections.content:
Many flat buyers assume that seeing a stamped initial building plan from RAJUK, CDA, KDA, or a Municipality guarantees full legality. In reality, construction compliance involves two separate approvals under the Dhaka Metropolitan Building (Construction, Development, Protection and Removal) Rules, 2008:

  • Construction Permit (নকশা অনুমোদন): Grants authority to construct a building strictly matching approved FAR (Floor Area Ratio), setback clearances, parking slots, and height limits.
  • Occupancy Certificate (অকুপেন্সি বা ব্যবহার সনদ): Issued after construction finishes and RAJUK/authority inspectors verify that as-built measurements match the sanctioned plan. Without an Occupancy Certificate, occupying the building is technically unlawful and exposes owners to utility disconnection notices and denial of clear apartment title verification.

sections.h2: BNBC 2020 Structural, Setback & High-Rise Fire Exit Requirements
sections.content:
Gazetted into enforceable law, the Bangladesh National Building Code (BNBC) 2020 sets non-negotiable engineering, structural load, electrical, and life-safety standards supervised by licensed architects, civil structural engineers, and MEP specialists across Dhaka and major urban municipalities:

  • Setback & Emergency Access: Mandatory front, side, and rear open setbacks ensuring fire-tender access and natural ventilation; illegal boundary-to-boundary construction violates BNBC and Building Construction Act Section 3.
  • High-Rise Fire Safety (Above 6 Storeys / 20 Meters): Buildings exceeding threshold heights require enclosed fire-rated staircases, pressurized lobbies, dedicated fire-water storage, sprinklers, automatic smoke detection, and unobstructed emergency exits.

sections.h2: Obtaining & Renewing a Fire Safety License Under the 2003 Act
sections.content:
Under Section 4 of the Fire Prevention and Extinction Act, 2003, operating a commercial office, garment factory, restaurant, warehouse, clinic, or storage facility without a valid Fire License from the Bangladesh Fire Service & Civil Defence (FSCD) is a punishable offense carrying imprisonment, heavy fines, and premises sealing.

  1. Pre-Construction Fire NOC: Required for multi-storey and commercial buildings before final RAJUK design clearance, alongside DoE environmental clearance compliance for factories and red-category projects.
  2. Annual Fire License & Inspection: Following installation of certified extinguishers, hydrant risers, and trained fire wardens, FSCD issues a building/business Fire License renewable annually upon inspection.

sections.h2: Risks for Flat Buyers, Commercial Tenants & Factory Owners Without Compliance
sections.content:
Non-compliance creates immediate financial liability for everyone in the chain:

  • Flat Buyers & NRB Investors: Developers who add unauthorized rooftop penthouses or swallow basement parking into commercial shops prevent the entire building from getting an Occupancy Certificate—blocking bank home loans, smooth flat registration, and fire insurance payouts. Verify land mutation and khatian title before signing booking deeds.
  • Corporate Tenants & Factories: Landlord non-compliance can invalidate commercial fire insurance policies and trigger sudden BIDA, Trade License, or environmental renewal refusals. Always insert a mandatory landlord warranty of Occupancy Certificate and valid Fire NOC inside commercial lease agreements.

sections.h2: Challenging Arbitrary Sealing or Utility Disconnection in Bangladesh Courts
sections.content:
Under Section 3B of the Building Construction Act, 1952, RAJUK or the Authorized Officer must serve a formal Show Cause Notice giving the owner a statutory opportunity to be heard before sealing premises or demolishing alleged deviations. Proper legal representation during administrative hearings frequently enables building owners to submit corrective structural retrofits, obtain fire-safety regularization, and avoid sudden business closures.

Where mobile courts or utility agencies act without statutory notice, fail to review regularized revised plans, or target innocent flat buyers, aggrieved owners can seek immediate stay orders via statutory appeal under Section 15 of the Act or a High Court Writ Petition against RAJUK action.

faqs.q: Is an Occupancy Certificate mandatory before buying a flat in Dhaka?
faqs.a: Yes. Under Dhaka building construction rules, a completed multi-storey building should not be legally occupied or permanently connected to utilities without a post-construction RAJUK Occupancy Certificate verifying that the actual structure complies with the sanctioned plan without unauthorized floors or setback violations.

faqs.q: Can I sue a developer if they built extra floors or blocked my parking space?
faqs.a: Yes. Under the Real Estate Development and Management Act, 2010 and the Specific Relief Act, flat buyers can pursue statutory complaints, arbitration, or civil injunctions against developers who deviate from the sanctioned RAJUK plan, build illegal rooftop units, or usurp allotted garage spaces.

faqs.q: Who needs a Fire Safety License in Bangladesh?
faqs.a: Under Section 4 of the Fire Prevention and Extinction Act, 2003, all factories, warehouses, commercial shopping malls, offices, restaurants, hospitals, schools, and premises storing flammable goods must obtain an annual Fire Safety License from Bangladesh Fire Service and Civil Defence upon physical inspection.

faqs.q: Can DESCO, WASA, or Titas cut utility lines if a building lacks RAJUK approval?
faqs.a: Yes. RAJUK routinely instructs electricity, gas, and water authorities to disconnect utility connections serving unauthorized structures; however, under Section 3B of the Building Construction Act, the enforcing authority must follow due process and issue prior written show-cause notice before coercive demolition or sealing.
